discovery: Discovery of magnetoelectric multiferroics and giant coupling between magnetism and ferroelectricity in complex oxides

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

motivation: Around 2003, Tokura (magnetically induced ferroelectricity in TbMnO3), Cheong (magnetic-field control of polarization in TbMn2O5 and the spin-frustration mechanism) and Ramesh (room-temperature multiferroic BiFeO3 thin films with large polarization) independently transformed a dormant curiosity into one of the most active fields of condensed matter physics. They showed that spin order can create electric polarization, and that electric fields can switch magnetism. This revealed new microscopic mechanisms such as spin-current and inverse Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling, topological vortex domains and conducting domain walls. Their work unified correlated-electron magnetism, ferroelectricity and oxide thin-film engineering. It opened routes to ultralow-power magnetoelectric memory and logic, and it seeded the wider study of emergent electromagnetic phenomena in quantum materials. This is a paradigm-creating discovery: a new field of physics whose concepts and materials are now taught and pursued worldwide.
